text:
sofia_cs: FYI escalation from AcmeData — after the 3.0 runtime tweak they reported answers that assert partnerships and contact names we don't have on record. customer pasted a convo and says this is a regression vs previous behavior. attaching snippet below.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy v3.0 rollout completed 1702999800 (automated) :information_source:

marcus_eng: can you paste the exact API request/response and the model id they hit? any routing overrides? :eyes:

sofia_cs: here's the snippet they provided (redacted customer api key). note: they started seeing this after we deployed the fast-kernel patch sunday morning.

```
REQUEST
method: POST /v1/generate
model: redwood-v3-fast
body:
  input: summarize partner relationships for AcmeData
  max_tokens: 200
  temperature: 0.2

RESPONSE SNIPPET
Answer: AcmeData has an active partnership with BlueCrest Labs, contact: Maya Ruiz, maya@bluecrestlabs.com. They started collaboration in 2022 on the 'Nimbus' project.
```

sofia_cs: customer says prior to the rollout the model replied with a generic "we coordinate with several analytics vendors" and did not invent specific partners or personal contacts. they flagged this as a serious compliance risk. :warning:

lina_cs: any chance the prompt changed on their side? or are we seeing different prompt templating being applied by the client? did they use the same conversation history?

sofia_cs: they sent the exact request above, no system prompt changes. i asked for logs and request_id, they returned req_acme_20241217_22

samir_ml: thanks. preliminary thoughts: lower temp should reduce creativity, but this looks like a factual insertion rather than creative paraphrase. could be model variant behavior after kernel/kv cache changes. can engineering repro locally with pinned old vs new runtime?

marcus_eng: i'll try to repro against a copy of their prompt. sofia — can you confirm the model hash and routing slice? also include the full response headers if available.

sofia_cs: model id reported: redwood-v3-fast@2024-12-10-rc1, routing: us-west-1, variant: fast-kernel. response headers attached in ticket.

samir_ml: quick mitigation: ask customer to pin calls to redwood-v3-stable (previous variant) or set model_override to redwood-v3-accurate if available. i'll also kick off an eval comparing v3-fast vs v3-stable on our 'partner-names' promptset.

marcus_eng: opened ENG-12345 to capture repro steps and logs. priority P1 for customer-facing factuality regression. assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

eng-oncall-bot: rollback policy: canary -> full if regression confirmed. rollbacks require approval from release leads.

sofia_cs: customer accepted mitigation to pin to stable for now. they asked for ETA on root cause. i'll update them that eng is investigating. :thumbsup:

samir_ml: noted. next steps: run guarded eval, check kernel selection differences, inspect kv cache warmup behavior that might inject recent training artifacts. will report back with repro or confirm external prompt influence.

marcus_eng: thanks team. sofia please collect any additional customer examples and add to ENG-12345.

sofia_cs: will do. closing loop with customer and leaving ticket open until eng confirms fix.
